blocks.text: My Tone Lab - PedalBoard
blocks.html: My Tone Lab - PedalBoard

blocks.text: This is my main guitar pedalboard, which I have built over the years while exploring various guitar tones and audio effects.
blocks.html: This is my main guitar pedalboard, which I have built over the years while exploring various guitar tones and audio effects.

blocks.text: By combining analog pedals with digital effects, it offers a wide range of sounds and flexible control for live performances and recording.
blocks.html: By combining analog pedals with digital effects, it offers a wide range of sounds and flexible control for live performances and recording.

blocks.text: In particular, I carefully designed the cable lengths and signal routing between effects to minimize potential signal degradation in the long signal chains. I also configured the buffers and routing with consideration for signal impedance and cable capacitance, while maintaining the flexibility of the system.

blocks.text: Effects Signal Chain

blocks.text: Input → Kill switch → Tuner/Buffer → Feedbacker → Compressor

blocks.text: → Modulation (Pre) → Noise Reduction (Send) → MIDI Controller (Drive Station) → Noise Reduction (Return) → Amp/Cab Sim

blocks.text: → Modulation (Post) → Delay → Reverb → Output

blocks.text: The diagram illustrates the overall signal flow of my pedalboard. The guitar signal first passes through a passive kill switch and an always-buffered tuner to maintain signal integrity. A feedback pedal is placed before downstream processing, followed by a compressor to shape the signal's dynamics.

blocks.text: Modulation Pre / Post mode. The Strymon Mobius uses its stereo inputs and outputs to support flexible Pre/Post routing, allowing modulation effects to be placed before or after the gain stage. Only one position can be active at a time.

blocks.text: Noise reduction G string loop. Conventional noise reduction can abruptly cut off sustain. To address this, the G-String loop isolates the high-gain section while using the clean guitar signal as a detection reference. This reduces noise while preserving natural sustain and decay.
blocks.html: Noise reduction G string loop. Conventional noise reduction can abruptly cut off sustain. To address this, the G-String loop isolates the high-gain section while using the clean guitar signal as a detection reference. This reduces noise while preserving natural sustain and decay.

blocks.text: MIDI / Control programmable architecture. To avoid excessive pedal switching during performances, I use a MIDI controller with seven analog loops for drive pedals. It also controls three digital processors through MIDI commands and tempo synchronization. A single preset can recall multiple drive combinations, digital effects settings, and tempo, allowing the entire system to function like a programmable multi-effects processor.
blocks.html: MIDI / Control programmable architecture. To avoid excessive pedal switching during performances, I use a MIDI controller with seven analog loops for drive pedals. It also controls three digital processors through MIDI commands and tempo synchronization. A single preset can recall multiple drive combinations, digital effects settings, and tempo, allowing the entire system to function like a programmable multi-effects processor.

blocks.text: Optional amp / cab stage. An amp simulator is placed after the drive section and before the spatial effects. For home recording or direct PA use, I typically use a Fender Deluxe Reverb-style clean amp simulation. When using a physical tube amplifier, I bypass this stage.

blocks.text: Post spatial chain. After modulation, delay and reverb shape the temporal and spatial characteristics of the sound. The dual-engine architecture of the Strymon MX series supports serial, parallel, and split configurations before the signal reaches the output.

blocks.text: I mainly favor the P pickup for a tight, full-bodied tone, using the J pickup to add brightness and sparkle. When I want a Jaco Pastorius-style tone, I use the J pickup alone.

blocks.text: I prefer a slightly darker overall tone, as the BB435 can sound a bit too bright for me.
